clue.text: Conserve flower left behind from romance

parts.note: the flower of something is its finest part, the pick of the bunch

indicators.note: the back end of the word romance supplies its closing letter

explanation.surface: Someone saves a bloom kept as a souvenir of a past love affair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flower' looks like a bloom but means the best part, as in 'the pick of the crop'.
explanation.definitionFit: To pickle food is to preserve it in vinegar or brine, a synonym for conserving it.

clue.text: Flower quietly presented to Auntie Dotty

parts.note: P (piano) is the musical marking for playing quietly

indicators.note: dotty means crazy, so the letters of Auntie go haywire

explanation.surface: A bloom is handed over without fuss to a slightly eccentric aunt.
explanation.walkthrough: 'presented to' is only a link; 'Dotty' turns the aunt's letters into ETUNIA, and 'Flower' here really is a bloom.
explanation.definitionFit: A petunia is a garden plant with trumpet-shaped blooms, an example of the class named.

clue.text: Savanna flowers

parts.note: a flower is something that flows, a river: the Cam runs through Cambridge
the Po is the great river of northern Italy, another 'flower'

explanation.surface: Blooms growing on a tropical grassland.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flowers' is crossword shorthand for rivers (things that flow); two of them, CAM and PO, sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: A campo is a stretch of open grassland in Brazil, the South American counterpart of savanna.

clue.text: Forthcoming opportunity for propositioning females?

parts.note: by tradition a woman may propose marriage on 29 February, an extra day that next came in 2012, soon after this puzzle appeared

explanation.surface: A coming chance for men to make advances to women.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests men propositioning women; the tradition is the reverse, women proposing on 29 February.
explanation.definitionFit: Folklore holds that on the extra February date of a quadrennial year, women may ask men to marry them.

clue.text: Foolish people shunned by Elizabeth's royal consort

indicators.note: the letter for Elizabeth avoids the word, so it is dropped from it

parts.note: wallies is British slang for silly, inept people
E is the initial of Elizabeth, as in the royal cypher ER

explanation.surface: Idiots are snubbed by the partner of Queen Elizabeth.
explanation.walkthrough: A WALLY is British slang for a fool. Wallis Simpson was the companion, later wife, of Edward VIII; the surface tempts you towards Prince Philip.
explanation.definitionFit: Wallis Simpson was the American divorcee for whom Edward VIII gave up the throne, the most famous royal partner.

clue.text: Akhmatova triumphantly captured part of one's heart

indicators.note: the two words hold the letters within them, as a prisoner is held

explanation.surface: The Russian poet Anna Akhmatova won someone's affection in style.
explanation.walkthrough: The run sits across 'AkhmatovA TRIUMphantly'.
explanation.definitionFit: An atrium is either of the two upper chambers of the heart, a piece of its anatomy.

clue.text: They go to court, employing good Latinist

indicators.note: taken here as putting the letters of good's initial and Latinist to fresh use in a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Parties in a lawsuit hire a capable classicist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'employing' is a loose anagram signal: G plus LATINIST rearranged; 'court' tempts a romantic reading.
explanation.definitionFit: Litigants are parties to a lawsuit, the people who appear before a judge in a legal dispute.

clue.text: Mouth kisses companion, provoking desire

indicators.note: one piece touches the next, as lips meet in a kiss, so they are joined end to end

parts.note: a stoma is a mouth-like opening in biology or surgery
CH is the abbreviation for Companion of Honour

explanation.surface: A kiss on the lips from a partner arouses passion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'kisses' only places the pieces side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: Having the stomach for something means having the appetite or inclination for it.

clue.text: Anonymous plea, having lost heart to radiant girl teen in Barking?

indicators.note: the central letter of the synonym is removed

parts.note: beamy means beaming or shining brightly
Val is a girl's name, short for Valerie

indicators.note: barking means barking mad, so the letters go wild

explanation.surface: An unsigned card sent to a glowing teenage girl who lives in Barking, a district of east London.
explanation.walkthrough: BEAMY loses its middle A; 'Barking' rearranges TEEN IN into ENTINE. Barking is also a place in London.
explanation.definitionFit: The words are the classic message on an unsigned card sent on 14 February, asking someone to be one's sweetheart.

clue.text: Couple emerging from exit seem half-cut

indicators.note: each word is cut in half and its back half kept

explanation.surface: A drunk-looking pair comes out of the exit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'half-cut' (British for tipsy) here keeps the back halves of EXIT and SEEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Two people in a relationship are referred to informally as an item.

clue.text: Lapse in control as 100 slashed from Scotsman's timber quota?

indicators.note: the hundred is cut away from the timber

parts.note: a caber is the tree trunk tossed at Highland games
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
a ration is a fixed allowance or share

explanation.surface: A Scotsman's allowance of wood is cut by a hundred, a slip of management.
explanation.walkthrough: Tossing the CABER is a Scottish sport at Highland games.
explanation.definitionFit: An aberration is a departure from normal, a temporary failure of self-command or judgement.

clue.text: Love in Florida limited by death's embrace

indicators.note: the end bounds the rest on both sides

parts.note: death is the end of life

indicators.note: the zero goes inside the state's abbreviation

parts.note: FL is the postal abbreviation for Florida
O is love, a zero score in tennis

explanation.surface: A romance in Florida is cut short by mortality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love' is the tennis zero; 'in' tucks it into the state abbreviation and 'limited by' wraps death around that, so the romance in the surface is pure decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: To enfold is to wrap in one's arms, so it is a synonym for hugging.

clue.text: Chew gum; annoy boyfriend

indicators.note: chewing mashes the letters of gum and annoy together into a new order

explanation.surface: Someone chewing gum irritates their partner.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone's young man is an old-fashioned phrase for the fellow they are going out with.

clue.text: Poor Mary, seduced by Lachlan, shedding a number of tears

indicators.note: the woman ends up in the arms of the man, so one piece goes inside the other
these letters are cast off from the man's name

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: poor signals the name Mary is in a bad way and comes out jumbled

explanation.surface: Unhappy Mary, led astray by a Scotsman, weeps.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a number' supplies two letters to remove from the Scottish name; 'Poor' scrambles the girl's name into RYMA, and 'seduced by' sets it inside what remains.
explanation.definitionFit: Lachrymal is the adjective for the eye's weeping, relating to the glands that produce teardrops.

clue.text: Spooner's kinkajou has rabbit fur

indicators.note: Dr Spooner swapped the opening sounds of word pairs

parts.note: a bunny is a child's word for a rabbit
hair is an animal's coat

explanation.surface: Spooner's tree-dwelling animal has a coat like a rabbit's.
explanation.walkthrough: Swapping the opening sounds of BUNNY HAIR gives the answer by sound.
explanation.definitionFit: The kinkajou, a tree-dwelling relative of the raccoon fond of nectar, is popularly called by this name.

clue.text: Including hand and part of foot

parts.note: inc. is the abbreviation for including

explanation.surface: Something takes in the hand and some of the foot, like a body part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'foot' is the twelve-unit length, not the body part.
explanation.definitionFit: A foot measures twelve of these units, so each is a fraction of that length.

clue.text: Affectionate airman with no date

parts.note: FO is Flying Officer, an RAF airman's rank
n.d. is the bibliographic abbreviation for no date

explanation.surface: A pilot feels loving although he has no one to go out with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no date' looks like a missing romantic partner; in bibliographies n.d. marks an undated source.
explanation.definitionFit: Being fond of someone means feeling warmth and liking towards them.

clue.text: See 17
Hard lass forewent mushy sentimentality

indicators.note: mushy means soft and pulpy, so the letters are mashed into a new order

explanation.surface: A tough girl gave up soppy romance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mushy' looks like part of the definition but is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names sugary, over-sweet romantic emotion, from the music that accompanies schmaltzy scenes.

clue.text: Writer's regret, having embraced quiet girl

indicators.note: the regret holds the other two pieces inside its arms

parts.note: to rue is to regret
sh is a call for quiet
Di is a girl's name, short for Diana

explanation.surface: An author is sorry he once hugged a shy young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface implies the writer has a regret; in fact 'having embraced' sets the hush and the short girl's name inside the regret word.
explanation.definitionFit: Salman Rushdie is the novelist who wrote Midnight's Children, so he is an example of an author.

clue.text: Sleep and food are what babies need

parts.note: a nap is a short sleep
pies are a kind of food

explanation.surface: Rest and nourishment are an infant's basic requirements.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is literally true of babies, which hides the definition in plain sight.
explanation.definitionFit: Babies need nappies, the British word for diapers, until they are toilet-trained.

clue.text: Pointlessly he goes looking for Cupid, perhaps

indicators.note: without points of the compass: south and east are removed

parts.note: a searcher is a person who looks for something

explanation.surface: Without much hope a man hunts for the god of love.
explanation.walkthrough: S and E are compass points, so 'Pointlessly' strips them from SEARCHER.
explanation.definitionFit: Cupid shoots arrows from a bow, so he is one example of a bowman.

clue.text: They say all Western artists regularly alluded to the Bible

indicators.note: signals a word as spoken, matching another spelling

parts.note: wholly means entirely, all

indicators.note: every other letter of artists is taken

explanation.surface: Western painters often made references to scripture.
explanation.walkthrough: WHOLLY sounds like HOLY; the second, fourth and sixth letters of ARTISTS give RIT.
explanation.definitionFit: Holy Writ is a phrase for Christian scripture, the sacred writings collected in the Bible.

clue.text: Removes clothes, initially shedding torrid tears

indicators.note: the opening letters of shedding and torrid are used

parts.note: rips are tears in cloth

explanation.surface: Someone undresses and, at first, cries passionately.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tears' reads as weeping but means rips.
explanation.definitionFit: To strip is to undress, taking off one's garments.

clue.text: They have reproductive hips and pink cheeks

definitions.meaning: a hip is the fruit of a rose bush, holding its seeds
a ruddy complexion is described as having ... in the cheeks

explanation.surface: Women with child-bearing hips and blushing faces.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hips' suggest the human body but are the seed-bearing fruits of the plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Rose bushes bear hips after flowering, and the flowers' colour lends its name to a healthy flush.

clue.text: Gave ring, then eloped abroad

indicators.note: abroad here means astray or all over the place, scattering the letters

explanation.surface: A couple called home, then ran away overseas to marry.
explanation.walkthrough: 'abroad' looks like a place but signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Giving someone a ring is British for calling them on the phone.

clue.text: Courting of female hearts?

definitions.meaning: ... in the old sense is the wooing of a woman
hearts are one of the four sets in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: Winning a woman's affections.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hearts' looks romantic but is a set of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: Suit means wooing, and it is also the name for each of the four card sets such as hearts.

clue.text: Froissart recounting imprisonment of French intellectual

indicators.note: the two words lock the letters inside them

explanation.surface: The medieval chronicler Froissart tells of a French thinker being jailed.
explanation.walkthrough: The run is 'froisSART REcounting'; Froissart was a 14th-century French chronicler.
explanation.definitionFit: Jean-Paul Sartre was the French existentialist philosopher, the archetype of a Parisian thinker.

clue.text: Poetry about lost love finally makes me nauseous
